records.rationale: Two masked randomized trials directly inform diagnosis after acute COVID, but COVID-OUT has an unresolved correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values. ACTIV-6’s secondary estimate is compatible with no difference and is affected by missing outcomes and unadjusted multiple comparisons. Low confidence reflects these unresolved limitations; the available results do not establish a settled prevention benefit.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Both trials used masked random allocation; selective extended follow-up in COVID-OUT and missing diagnosis outcomes in ACTIV-6 limit the comparisons.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Both concern prevention during acute infection, not treatment of established Long COVID; their populations and diagnosis follow-up times differ.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: COVID-OUT’s provisional hazard ratio is 0.59 (95% CI 0.39–0.89); ACTIV-6’s difference is −0.7 percentage points (95% credible interval −1.5 to 0.1).

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: The point estimates both favor metformin, but two differently defined follow-ups with different uncertainty do not establish a replicated common effect.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: COVID-OUT’s indexed correction and conflicting control percentages remain unresolved; ACTIV-6 has only a partial full-text record. The diagnosis synthesis remains on hold.

records.rationale: ACTIV-6 supplies a large masked randomized comparison for the prespecified six-month symptom-or-death outcome, so the finding is more informative than an uncontrolled symptom report. The trial did not meet its efficacy threshold, and the interval permits both benefit and a small increase. Missing symptom outcomes and incomplete access to the full methods reduce editorial confidence to Moderate, rather than demonstrating treatment equivalence.

domains.name: Directness

domains.name: Precision

records.rationale: A double-blind randomized comparison directly tests recovery after established Long COVID, but only the abstract is available for this assessment. Recovery occurred in 84 of 132 metformin recipients and 90 of 132 placebo recipients, without an extracted between-group uncertainty interval. Low confidence reflects incomplete methods and precision information; the reported absence of improvement does not establish equivalence.

domains.name: Precision

records.rationale: STOP-PASC directly tests persistent symptoms using a masked randomized comparison and did not demonstrate benefit on its primary pooled severity outcome. The 155-person, single-center trial stopped early for futility, and the available outcome record lacks a numerical pooled effect interval. Those limitations support Moderate editorial confidence in the bounded finding, while leaving smaller effects and other regimens unresolved.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Double-blind random allocation supports the primary comparison; early futility stopping and possible unmasking from taste disturbance limit confidence in self-reported symptoms.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The comparison applies to the studied 15-day course and six pooled core symptom groups at week 10; both arms received ritonavir.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The available evidence records no significant primary difference but no numerical pooled interval; exact effect size and the range of compatible smaller effects remain unquantified.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: This row contains one trial family. Its separate fatigue analysis uses the same participants and does not count as replication.

records.rationale: The randomized STOP-PASC comparison provides direct fatigue data, but fatigue was a secondary measure in a small trial that stopped early. The estimate of 0.38 points has an interval from −2.40 to 3.15, and the endpoint-specific analyzed denominators are not recorded. These precision and reporting limits, alongside multiple symptom comparisons, make confidence Low for the fatigue effect rather than proving no effect.

domains.name: Directness

records.rationale: RECOVER-VITAL is a large masked randomized trial, but the available evidence supports the combined phenotype assessment only through its abstract. Different symptom groups use different primary outcomes, and no phenotype-specific effect sizes or uncertainty intervals are extracted here. Low confidence reflects those missing details; the abstract’s negative primary finding is not proof of equal outcomes across every phenotype.

domains.name: Study methods

domains.name: Directness

records.rationale: This randomized, masked Parkinson pilot directly measured UPDRS, but its clinical comparison is based on a small per-protocol sample over three months. The between-group result was not significant, and an uncertainty interval is not recorded. Withdrawals, short follow-up and imprecision reduce confidence to Low; improvement within the metformin arm and biomarker differences do not establish clinical superiority.

domains.name: Study methods

domains.name: Directness

domains.name: Precision

records.rationale: Vorinostat was nominated from transcriptome and Connectivity Map analysis rather than administered to people with Crohn disease. The enrichment score cannot quantify symptom improvement, remission or clinical safety, and the analysis relies on one selected dataset. Confidence is Low for clinical inference; this is a hypothesis requiring experimental and human confirmation, not demonstrated treatment benefit.

records.rationale: Clomipramine was nominated by a gene-expression matching analysis, without treating patients or measuring Crohn symptom improvement. The score is a computational ranking rather than a clinical effect, and the single-dataset analysis requires external experimental confirmation. Confidence is Low for clinical inference; the finding does not establish remission, safety or a reason to prescribe clomipramine for Crohn disease.

records.rationale: Random allocation and blinded cognitive evaluation support the reported 24-week MCCB score improvement with adjunctive metformin. Confidence is Moderate because the small trial was open-label without placebo, 59 of 72 participants completed follow-up, and the practical importance of the score difference remains uncertain. The positive interval supports this test-score finding, not proof of improved everyday functioning or broad schizophrenia benefit.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: The evaluator-blinded trial randomized 72 participants but did not blind patients with placebo. Attrition and treatment expectations can still affect the comparison.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The endpoint is a cognitive-test composite in young, clinically stable patients with relatively recent schizophrenia receiving antipsychotics; everyday function was not established by this assessment.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The estimated difference is +3.43 MCCB points (95% CI 1.83–5.02). The exact mixed-model analysis denominator and meaningful-change threshold are not separately verified.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: One parent trial supports the finding. Its metabolomic and MRI companion report shares participants and must not be counted as replication.

domains.name: Source integrity

records.rationale: MET-PREVENT directly assessed walking speed in a masked placebo-controlled trial, with complete follow-up recorded for 70 of 72 randomized participants. Its near-zero estimate and interval support no demonstrated improvement over four months, while leaving smaller differences possible. Moderate confidence reflects the small, narrowly selected older population and abstract-level access; the result does not establish equivalence or describe younger adults.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Double-blind random allocation and near-complete outcome follow-up support comparison; the complete report is still needed to assess adherence and other analytical decisions.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Walking speed was directly measured in older adults with probable sarcopenia and frailty, predominantly White British and averaging 80.4 years; applicability beyond this setting is limited.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The adjusted difference is +0.001 m/s (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06). This is a bounded estimate around zero, not a formal demonstration of equivalence.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: One trial family supports this particular frailty and walking-speed question; broader replication is not established by this selected record.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: Only the primary abstract and its repository copy support this assessment. The available participant counts and interval do not replace full-text and supplement assessment.

records.rationale: PRINCIPLE directly compared doxycycline with usual care in community patients and found no clinically meaningful improvement in recovery or hospitalization outcomes. Random allocation is informative, but the open-label design can affect self-reported recovery and the severe-outcome estimate is less precise. Moderate confidence applies to these selected acute-COVID outcomes; it does not establish exact equivalence or address prophylaxis.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: The randomized community platform trial was open-label. Knowledge of treatment is particularly relevant to the self-reported recovery component.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The studied patients were older or clinically vulnerable with suspected or confirmed acute COVID; the comparison concerns community treatment over 28 days.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The primary report’s recovery and hospitalization intervals include no difference. Hospitalization or death was relatively uncommon, so smaller severe-outcome effects remain uncertain.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: One PRINCIPLE trial family supplies both outcomes; reporting two endpoints does not create two independent replications.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: The available primary-publication summary supports the reported outcomes. Full methods and supplement detail are insufficiently represented for a complete assessment of reporting limitations.

records.rationale: A randomized comparison in recurrent glioblastoma directly tests adding disulfiram and copper to chemotherapy and shows no significant survival improvement with more severe toxicity. Confidence is Moderate because the trial is small and survival precision is limited, even though the toxicity signal is clinically relevant. This assessment concerns the tested combination, not disulfiram alone or all cancers.

domains.name: Directness

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: Grade 3 or higher events were reported in 34% versus 11%; the nonsignificant survival comparison does not establish equivalent survival.

domains.name: Consistency

domains.name: Source integrity

records.rationale: Responses in nine patients receiving propranolol plus pembrolizumab are preliminary observations from a dose-escalation study. Without a control group, the 78% response rate cannot separate propranolol’s contribution from that of the active immunotherapy. The very small sample and exploratory efficacy objective make confidence Low for an added melanoma treatment benefit.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Tumor response is clinically relevant, but every participant received pembrolizumab; the design cannot directly estimate the additional effect of propranolol.

domains.name: Precision

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: A single small dose-escalation study supports this combination observation; no independent controlled replication is included in the row.

domains.name: Source integrity

records.rationale: The randomized, double-blind gemcitabine comparison directly tested whether adding simvastatin delayed progression in advanced pancreatic cancer. The reported medians of 2.4 versus 3.6 months did not show a significant advantage, but the 114-person phase II sample and lack of an extracted between-group interval limit conclusions about smaller effects. Moderate confidence applies to the tested combination and disease setting, without asserting equivalence.

domains.name: Directness

domains.name: Precision

domains.name: Consistency

A published correction affects plasma-concentration reporting; no uncorrected exposure value is used to justify this outcome assessment.

records.rationale: RECOVERY provides a large randomized comparison with an objective 28-day mortality endpoint and near-complete recorded follow-up. The rate ratio of 1.09 (95% CI 0.97–1.23) excludes a substantial mortality reduction in the studied hospitalized population, giving High editorial confidence in the bounded negative finding. The interval still permits a small reduction and increased mortality, so this is not a claim of exact equivalence or a conclusion about prevention.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: The large randomized trial was open-label, but mortality is less susceptible to expectation effects than subjective symptoms; follow-up forms were available for 99.5% in both groups.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: The endpoint directly measures all-cause death by day 28 among hospitalized COVID patients receiving hydroxychloroquine or usual care; it does not test prophylaxis.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The 1,561 versus 3,155 patient comparison gives a mortality rate ratio of 1.09 (95% CI 0.97–1.23), ruling out a substantial relative mortality benefit in this setting.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: This grade rests on the strength of the specified large randomized result; independent replication is not inferred from multiple reports or subgroup analyses of the same trial.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: The primary report supports the mortality estimate and follow-up completeness. No unresolved correction affecting this endpoint is identified in the sources checked.

Confidence is Low for the treatment effect despite the randomized design, and the result does not establish equivalent efficacy.

Its single-arm design cannot separate the added drug from continued imatinib response, patient selection or time. The small sample, molecular rather than clinical endpoint and incomplete methods and precision records keep this exploratory finding at Low.

records.rationale: The randomized phase III comparison provides direct evidence of worse outcomes with thalidomide than tamoxifen in biochemical-only recurrence: the mortality hazard ratio was 1.76 with a 95% interval of 1.16–2.68, alongside substantially more severe toxicity. The study enrolled 139 women and closed after an interim analysis failed to show reduced recurrence, which limits confidence and precision beyond this comparison. The narrow recurrence setting and abstract-based methods verification prevent a High grade; the harmful direction itself does not lower evidence strength.

domains.name: Directness
